title: Chemistry Discoveries — Louis Pasteur

competencies.text: Report how Louis Pasteur combined chemistry and biology to understand disease and prevent infection.

days.title: Who Was Louis Pasteur?
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will report how Louis Pasteur combined chemistry and biology to understand disease and prevent infection.

🧑‍🔬 From Crystals to Germs

Louis Pasteur (1822–1895) was a French chemist. He first studied crystals and discovered that some molecules come in mirror-image forms. Wine makers then asked him why their wine sometimes turned sour. Using a microscope, he found that living yeast causes normal fermentation, while other microorganisms spoil it.

That discovery led him to a powerful idea: if tiny organisms can spoil wine and milk, maybe tiny organisms also cause disease. He spent the rest of his life testing that idea — combining the careful measurement of chemistry with the living world of biology.

🏆 His Major Contributions

ContributionWhat it showed or did
Fermentation studiesLiving yeast, not "chemical decay," causes fermentation
Swan-neck flask experimentDisproved spontaneous generation
Germ theory of diseaseMicroorganisms cause infectious disease
PasteurizationGentle heating kills harmful microbes in liquids
VaccinesWeakened germs train the body to resist anthrax and rabies

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: Pasteur was trained as a chemist. Why is he also called a founder of microbiology?

choices.label: He showed that microbes cause fermentation and disease
He invented the very first glass microscope ever made
He discovered the chemical formula of water
He proved that diseases come from bad air

scenario.explanation: Pasteur used chemistry methods to study living microorganisms and showed their role in fermentation, spoilage and disease — the core of microbiology.

scenario.text: What did Pasteur discover about wine that turned sour?

choices.label: Unwanted microorganisms had grown in it
The grapes had far too much natural sugar
The barrels let in too much sunlight
The wine had cooled down too quickly

scenario.explanation: Healthy fermentation is done by yeast; when other microbes grow, the wine spoils. This linked microbes to spoilage and later to disease.

scenario.text: Which combination BEST describes Pasteur's approach?

choices.label: Chemistry methods applied to living things
Physics formulas applied to the stars
Biology facts copied from older science books
Mathematics used to predict typhoons

scenario.explanation: He brought careful chemical experiments and measurements to questions about microorganisms — joining chemistry and biology.

days.title: Germ Theory and the Swan-Neck Flask
days.content:
❓ The Old Idea: Spontaneous Generation

For centuries people believed that living things could arise from non-living matter — maggots from rotting meat, microbes from broth. Diseases were blamed on "bad air" (miasma).

🧪 Pasteur's Swan-Neck Flask Experiment

  1. He boiled broth in a flask with a long, S-shaped neck. Boiling killed the microbes already in it.
  2. Air could still enter, but dust and microbes were trapped in the curve of the neck.
  3. The broth stayed clear for months.
  4. When he tilted the flask so broth touched the trapped dust, or broke the neck, the broth quickly became cloudy with microbes.

Conclusion: microbes come only from other microbes, not from the broth or the air itself. The experiment was fair because air could reach the broth in both cases — only the microbes were kept out.

🦠 Germ Theory

If microbes come from other microbes, then infections spread when germs pass from person to person. This explains why handwashing, boiling water and sterilizing tools prevent disease.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each idea to its meaning. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.why: This old belief was disproved by Pasteur's experiment.

match.right: Lets air in but traps dust and microbes
match.why: Only microbes were kept out, so air alone could not be blamed.
The test then shows whether new microbes appear by themselves.

match.right: Broth touches trapped dust and turns cloudy
match.why: Microbes from the dust grew once they reached the broth.
It replaced the idea that disease comes from bad air.

match.right: Yeast turns sugar into alcohol and CO₂
match.why: Pasteur showed fermentation is done by living yeast.
Germ theory explains why it prevents infection.
It prevents germs from entering wounds.

days.title: Pasteurization
days.content:
🥛 What Pasteurization Is

Pasteurization heats a liquid to a set temperature for a set time to kill most harmful microorganisms while keeping the taste and nutrients. It does not boil the liquid and does not kill every microbe, so pasteurized milk still needs refrigeration.

MethodTemperature and timeResult
LTLT (batch)63 °C for 30 minutesSmall dairies; keep cold
HTST72 °C for 15 secondsMost fresh milk; keep cold
UHT135 °C for 2–4 secondsShelf-stable boxed milk until opened

🔬 Why It Works

Heat denatures the proteins of bacteria — their enzymes lose shape and stop working, so the cells die. This is chemistry (proteins and heat) solving a biology problem (harmful microbes).

🇵🇭 In Our Communities

Fresh carabao milk from a local farm spoils in a day or two at room temperature. Pasteurized milk lasts longer in the refrigerator, and UHT milk lasts months unopened. Pasteurization also protects against Salmonella, E. coli and Listeria.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Apply germ theory and pasteurization. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: A sari-sari store sells fresh carabao milk that spoils in 2 days, while boxed UHT milk lasts for months. What BEST explains the difference?

choices.label: UHT heating killed nearly all microbes in the box
Fresh milk has much less water than UHT milk
Boxed milk contains extra sugar as a preservative
Carabao milk is naturally less nutritious

scenario.explanation: UHT milk was heated to about 135 °C and sealed, so almost no microbes remain to spoil it. Raw milk still contains bacteria that multiply quickly.

scenario.text: A dairy wants to keep its milk's fresh taste but make it safe. Which choice is BEST?

choices.label: HTST: 72 °C for 15 seconds, then chill
Boil the milk for 30 minutes, then chill
Keep the raw milk cold, with no heating
Add vinegar to the milk to sour it quickly

scenario.explanation: HTST kills harmful microbes with a short heating, so flavor and nutrients are kept. Long boiling changes taste; cold alone does not kill germs.

scenario.text: In the swan-neck experiment, why did Pasteur let AIR reach the broth?

choices.label: To show air alone did not create microbes
To feed the growing microbes with fresh oxygen
To cool the broth faster after boiling
To make the broth evaporate quickly

scenario.explanation: Supporters of spontaneous generation said air contained a 'life force.' Letting air in while trapping dust proved that the microbes, not the air, were needed.

scenario.text: A nurse washes her hands between patients. Which of Pasteur's ideas does this practice apply?

choices.label: Germ theory of disease
Spontaneous generation
Mirror-image crystals
Bad-air (miasma) theory

scenario.explanation: Germ theory says microbes cause infection and spread from person to person. Handwashing removes them before they reach the next patient.

scenario.text: Pasteurized milk was left on a table overnight and turned sour. Which explanation is MOST accurate?

choices.label: Pasteurization reduces microbes but does not remove all
Pasteurized milk has no microbes, so the air soured it
The heat of pasteurization made the milk unstable
Milk always sours at night because of moonlight

scenario.explanation: Pasteurization kills most harmful microbes, not all. The few survivors (and any new ones) multiply quickly at room temperature, so the milk must stay cold.

days.title: Vaccines and Pasteur's Legacy
days.content:
💉 The First Lab-Made Vaccines

Pasteur noticed that chickens injected with an old, weakened culture of cholera bacteria did not get sick — and later resisted fresh, strong bacteria. He used the same idea to make vaccines for anthrax (in livestock, 1881) and rabies (1885), first used on a boy bitten by a rabid dog.

🛡️ How Vaccines Work

A vaccine contains a weakened or killed germ, or part of it. It cannot cause the disease, but the immune system learns to recognize it and makes memory cells. If the real germ attacks later, the body responds quickly. This is immunity.

🇵🇭 Today

  • Rabies is still a danger from dog and cat bites in the Philippines. Washing the wound with soap and water and getting post-exposure vaccination at an animal bite center saves lives.
  • The national immunization program protects children against measles, polio and other diseases.

🧠 Pasteur's Lesson for Scientists

"Chance favors the prepared mind." Careful observation, fair experiments and testing an idea until the evidence is clear turned a chemist's questions into discoveries that still save millions of lives.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: Which old belief did the swan-neck flask experiment disprove?

choices.label: Spontaneous generation
Germ theory of disease
Conservation of mass
The cell theory of life

escape.explanation: The experiment showed that microbes come from other microbes, not from non-living broth — disproving spontaneous generation.

escape.text: What does pasteurization do to milk?

choices.label: Kills most harmful microbes using heat
Removes all the fat from the milk
Adds extra vitamins and minerals to the milk
Turns the milk into cheese quickly

escape.explanation: Pasteurization heats milk to a set temperature for a set time, killing most harmful microorganisms while keeping its taste and nutrients.

escape.text: How does heat kill bacteria during pasteurization?

choices.label: It denatures the bacteria's proteins
It dissolves the bacteria in the water
It freezes the bacteria's enzymes
It turns the bacteria into sugar

escape.explanation: Heat changes the shape of bacterial proteins and enzymes so they stop working, and the cells die.

choices.label: A weakened, killed or partial germ
A strong, active form of the disease
Antibiotics that kill every germ
Vitamins that replace the immune system

escape.explanation: A vaccine has a harmless form or part of the germ so the immune system can learn to recognize it without getting sick.

escape.text: A student is bitten by a stray dog. Based on Pasteur's work, what is the BEST action?

choices.label: Wash the wound and get rabies vaccine shots
Wait to see whether the dog gets sick first
Cover the wound and apply only a cold pack
Drink plenty of milk to build up immunity

escape.explanation: Rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms appear. Washing the wound and starting post-exposure vaccination right away prevents the disease.

escape.text: Which statement BEST shows how Pasteur combined chemistry and biology?

choices.label: He used heat chemistry to kill living microbes
He measured the speed of light in water
He sorted all the elements into a periodic table
He invented the steam engine for factories

escape.explanation: Pasteurization uses a chemical effect of heat (denaturing proteins) to solve a biological problem (harmful microbes).
